info.title: Aurora Listener API
info.description: In-development, path-free API for Aurora web and future dedicated listener applications. Administrative and library-management operations remain outside v1.

listenerAuth.description: Aurora web JWT or a dedicated aurora_app_ listener key.

editionLabel.description: Edition or release variant such as "Deluxe Edition", when the album is one of several editions.

tracks.description: Credited tracks first, then tracks on albums the artist owns as album artist without a performer credit.

ownedAlbums.description: Albums owned by the Various Artists pseudo-artist. Always empty for real artists.

ownerClientId.description: Deprecated: the client that last created or claimed the session. A session belongs to its user; any of their devices may change it.

id.description: The device that plays the session (its client ID).

kind.description: browser: the device plays the session itself. cast: the device sends it to a Cast device it controls; `name` is the Cast device's. receiver: the Cast receiver plays the session itself, with its own credential; a controller claims it, and `name` is the Cast device's.

generation.description: Grant generation; goes up on every claim.

castSessionId.description: kind cast: the Cast session the output sends to; kind receiver: the Cast session the receiver runs in. When the server knows it (it is not kept across a server restart).

status.description: active: reporting. unreachable: silent for over a minute, last state kept; only a report or a new claim changes it. ended: the output itself reported stopped, idle or error.

queueEntryId.description: The entry the output is playing. Position belongs to this entry only.

reportedAt.description: Server time the report was accepted; interpolate from here while playing.

volume.description: The output's volume, 0 to 1, when it reports one (not kept across a server restart; the next report brings it back).

output.description: The device currently playing the session, if any.

infinity.description: Infinity: the server keeps a few upcoming entries, chosen by the recommendation engine, while something plays the session.

visibility.description: Who may join (Listen together): private (nobody), invite (with a join link), discoverable (nearby users too).

access.description: The caller's access: the owner (every scope, and alone chooses where it plays) or a guest with its scopes.

addedBy.description: infinity: an Infinity pick (by the server, or a client that chose it itself). user: anything else. Clients show Infinity picks apart until they play.

token.description: Output credential: a short-lived token bound to this session and grant. Keep it in memory only. For a receiver output, a receiver credential, which the receiver itself uses.

renewableUntil.description: Receiver credentials only: the receiver may renew its own credential (POST …/output/renew) until then, 24 hours after a controller issued it.

mediaToken.description: Renewals only (POST …/output/renew): a fresh 12-hour media token for the receiver's stream and artwork URLs, so it never needs the owner's login media token.

accepted.description: True when sent to the output; false for a repeated requestId.

clientId.description: The device's client ID (X-Aurora-Client-Id, or the event stream's clientId).

name.description: The name the device gave itself ("Chrome on Linux"), when it gave one.

kind.description: browser: the web app. receiver: a Cast receiver following a session. app: another API v1 client.

pictureUrl.description: Always null for now; when set, a URL on this server.

path.description: The join page on this server: /listen/<token>. Anyone signed in on this server who opens it can join.

guests.description: The guests' avatars only: no names, and nothing about what plays, before joining.

joined.description: The caller is already in this session (its owner, or a guest).

accepted.description: False when the report was older than one already accepted (by seq) and was dropped.

subsonicProviderLoveSyncEnabled.description: Mirror stars from OpenSubsonic clients to Last.fm and MusicBrainz. Defaults to true.

newBrowseEnabled.description: Browse by Aurora's genres and styles instead of the old genre list (preview). Defaults to false.

tagCount.description: Their genre tags that match no genre or style.

styles.description: The 3 styles with the most tracks.

artworkIds.description: Covers of up to 4 albums that are most this genre.

styles.description: Every style with tracks, most tracks first.

noStyleTrackCount.description: Tracks in the genre without a specific style.

countries.description: The countries with at least 3 tracks here, most tracks first, at most 12.

vocals.description: Female and male vocals by the artists' tags, with at least 3 tracks.

moods.description: Moods by the artists' tags with at least 3 tracks here, most tracks first.

share.description: Share of the album's tracks in this genre or style.

trackCount.description: Its tracks in this genre or style.

share.description: Share of the artist's music in this genre or style, each album counted once.

decade.description: 1990 for the 1990s: by the original release year, else the year, else the artist's era tag.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: where the artists are from (MusicBrainz, artist tags, or the release country).

value.description: vocals: female or male; mood: chill, party, uplifting, melancholic, dark, atmospheric, romantic, energetic or funky.

countries.description: The countries with at least 3 tracks here, most tracks first, at most 12.

vocals.description: Female and male vocals by the artists' tags, with at least 3 tracks.

moods.description: Moods by the artists' tags with at least 3 tracks here, most tracks first.

soundsCloseTo.description: The styles that sound nearest, from any genre, nearest first (by the centroids of their tagged tracks' audio embeddings). Empty until the style has a centroid: at least 8 tagged tracks by 3 artists.

label.description: "Trip Hop · Electronic", or the genre name.

matchedAlias.description: The tag that matched when it was not the name ("Drum & Bass").

tags.description: Genre tags on tracks without a genre, most tracks first.

untaggedTrackCount.description: Tracks without a genre and without any genre tag.

entries.description: Genres and styles of at least 20 % of the album's tracks, or among its 3 strongest; strongest first.
As for albums, with each of the artist's albums counted once.

listenerTags.description: What listeners tag the artist with on Last.fm and MusicBrainz; empty without provider data.

role.description: artist and featured (the billed artists, from the artist tag), then composer, producer, lyricist, performer, …

artistId.description: null for a billed name the library has no artist for.

detail.description: An instrument for performers, when known.

imageUrl.description: A stored artist image, when the library has one (no provider lookup).

credits.description: Every stored credit, in role order (performer, composer, conductor, lyricist, producer, …).

tags.description: The genre tags in the file, as written.

source.description: tag: a genre tag in the file; audio: the sound; artist: the artist's tags on Last.fm or MusicBrainz; override: set by hand.

fromTags.description: With source tag: the file tags that map here.

disputed.description: A tagged style the sound contradicts (a near-zero score, and far from the style's other tracks): kept, but waiting for an admin to Keep or Remove it.

styles.description: The track's genres and styles, genre rows first, strongest first.

closestStyles.description: The 12 styles the audio model scores highest (raw scores, 0-1; a track can score high on several).

genreMix.description: Each genre's share of the summed scores over all 400 styles, largest first.

sound.description: null before analysis, or for a track analysed without real audio.

artworkId.description: Cover art of the album, as for AlbumSummary.

role.description: artist: billed alongside the track's own artist.

otherArtists.description: The other billed artists, the featured artists and the remixers, in that order, each once; only artists in the library, at most 10.

styles.description: Styles whose centroids sit nearest the track's sound, its own styles left out, nearest first.

tracks.description: The nearest tracks by sound: none from its album or recording, one version of a song, at most two per artist; up to 12.

soundsCloseTo.description: null for a track without a real audio embedding.

otherAlbums.description: Other albums in the library with this recording (by MusicBrainz recording id, else artist and title).

id.description: The calling client: the X-Aurora-Client-Id it sent, or a server-assigned id.

links.description: Each artwork ID with its signed link (`/api/v1/artwork/<id>?sig=…`), which opens that one image with no credential.

ids.description: Artwork IDs (a track's artworkId) to sign links for.

skipped.description: True when nothing was generated, for example because a refresh is already running or no LLM is configured.

reason.description: Why no radio can be built, when not eligible.

sessionHistoryTrackIds.description: Playback-start history, oldest to newest, including the playing track. Merged after older server history; does not record plays.

exclude.description: Track IDs already queued or otherwise excluded. Exclusions survive similarity relaxation and fallback.

seedTrackIds.description: The end of the play queue, oldest to newest, ending with the track the recommendation will follow. When present it steers the recommendation instead of playback history; history still prevents repeats. Only the last 10 are used.

genreStrictness.description: Style match: how much sharing styles with the queue lifts a close-sounding track (β from 0 to 0.2). Changing genre never counts against a track.

InfinitySettings.description: Per-request overrides for saved user tuning. Omitted values use saved settings or engine defaults.

requestId.description: Idempotency key for the whole patch; kept 24 hours.

entryIds.description: Client-proposed queue entry IDs, one unique UUID per track. Omitted, the server generates them.

index.description: Legacy position form. Give exactly one of index or afterEntryId.

afterEntryId.description: Insert after this entry; null inserts at the head. Give exactly one of index or afterEntryId.

entryIds.description: Client-proposed queue entry IDs, one unique UUID per track. Omitted, the server generates them.

addedBy.description: Mark the inserted entries as Infinity picks (`infinity`). Default `user`.

toIndex.description: Legacy position form. Give exactly one of toIndex or afterEntryId.

afterEntryId.description: Move after this entry; null moves to the head. Give exactly one of toIndex or afterEntryId.

kind.description: browser: the device plays the session itself. cast: the device sends it to a Cast device it controls; `name` is the Cast device's. receiver: the Cast receiver plays the session itself, with its own credential; a controller claims it, and `name` is the Cast device's.

castSessionId.description: kind cast: the Cast session this device sends to, so another device can tell joining it from starting a new one. kind receiver (required): the Cast session the receiver runs in; the output ID becomes `receiver:<castSessionId>`.

seq.description: Increases with every report within one grant; a report not above the last accepted one is dropped.

volume.description: The output's volume, 0 to 1. Optional; an output that sends it can be given setVolume commands.

outputId.description: Optional; must match the output credential.

outputGeneration.description: Optional; must match the output credential.

requestId.description: A repeated requestId is accepted once.

outputId.description: The output this command is for: the session's current output.id.

outputGeneration.description: Its current output.generation; a newer claim makes the command stale.

entryId.description: Play this queue entry from its start.

oneOf.description: Change the output's volume. Sent only to an output that reports its volume.

revision.description: The output first adopts the session queue at this revision or later.

entryId.description: Then plays this entry from its start.

visibility.description: private: nobody can join (guests already in stay) and every join link stops working; invite: anyone with a join link can; discoverable: also users nearby (the same public address as one of the owner's devices).

permissions.description: The guests' permissions, for the working links and every guest already in, at once. The web app offers three stacked levels: Queue Editor [queue], Playback Control [queue, transport], Music Manager [queue, transport, replace].
What joining through the link grants; all scopes when left out.

userIds.description: Users of this server to prompt; each hears playbackSession.invitePrompt on /events.

targetClientId.description: A device from GET /devices: it takes the session over and plays it from where it is.

patch.summary: Who may join, and what guests may do (owner)
patch.description: Private keeps guests already in, but no one new can join, and every join link stops working: opening the session again takes a new link. Discoverable also shows it to users nearby (GET /playback-sessions/nearby). New permissions apply to the working links and to every guest at once. Guests hear playbackSession.visibilityChanged and playbackSession.accessChanged (`{sessionId, permissions}`); users nearby hear playbackSession.discoverable (`{sessionId, discoverable}`, live only).

get.description: Use a short-lived sse token (or a receiver credential, which hears only its own session) in the query string because EventSource cannot set Authorization headers; a full session token is refused. Each event's data is JSON `{id, type, occurredAt, data}`. Types: playbackSession.created / updated / handedOff / deleted (fetch the session when its revision is newer), playbackSession.progress (every accepted output report: `{sessionId, revision, outputId, generation, report}`; live only, never replayed), playlist.changed, annotation.changed, playbackSession.command (to the output: `{sessionId, outputId, generation, requestId, issuedBy, command}`; live only), playbackSession.transferRequested (to the device asked to take over: `{sessionId, revision, targetClientId, requestedBy}`; live only), Listen together: playbackSession.memberJoined (`{sessionId, userId, avatar}`), memberLeft (`{sessionId, userId, reason: left | removed | ended}`), visibilityChanged (`{sessionId, visibility}`), togetherEnded (`{sessionId}`) and accessChanged (`{sessionId, permissions}`), to the owner and its guests; discoverable (`{sessionId, discoverable}`, live only) to users nearby; and invitePrompt (`{sessionId, token, path, preview}`, to a prompted user), devices.changed (`{devices}`: every device of this user with Aurora open, whenever one opens or closes; live only), cast.status (`{castSessionId, status}`: the status of a Cast receiver, to the user whose media it plays, with sync on or off; live only), library.revision, playbackSync.changed (`{enabled}`: whether the playback-session API works for this account now), and resync.required (the replay window was lost: re-fetch everything).
